The Two Siemens Stories Investors Had In Front Of Them

The shares cost €227 at the start of the period, and Siemens investors were weighing two very different but plausible stories.

On the bullish side, one Narrative saw Fair Value at €246, 9% above the start price, built on 6.1% annual revenue growth and profit margins reaching 11.2% within about three years.

The more cautious view put Fair Value at €208, 8% below the start price, assuming 5.0% yearly revenue growth, a 17.0% profit margin over five years, and a future P/E of 18.0x.

What The Results Changed For The Siemens Argument

Siemens later reported Q4 2026 revenue of €23,683m and net income of €2,191m, with net margin at 9.3% versus 7.7% a year earlier. That mix of higher sales, higher profit and a wider margin leaned toward the bullish case that expected healthier profitability, although it did not directly test the specific 11.2% or 17.0% margin targets yet.

The useful takeaway is simple. When a thesis hinges on better margins, track net margin alongside revenue and earnings in each report and check whether it is actually creeping toward the level the story needs.

Siemens trades at €279 after a 23.9% gain over the past year. The bullish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St sees Fair Value above that level based on a stronger mix from Smart Infrastructure and industrial software partnerships rather than just broad AI excitement.

It also sells transformers, grid gear and software that move electricity from plant to plug. That matters as AI projects and electrification plans demand tougher, smarter grids.

data.title: What Greencore Group Doubters Overlooked
data.description:

Investors who held Greencore Group over the past year are up 35.1%, including dividends. The Two Stories Investors Had To Choose Between On Greencore Group

The shares cost £2.29 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Greencore Group then had to decide which story felt closer to reality.

On the optimistic side, one narrative pointed to a Fair Value of £2.56, a rough guide to what the price might be if the thesis played out. That view leaned on the Making Business Easier program and a wider technology overhaul, which were expected to cut costs and lift future efficiency.

The more cautious narrative anchored on a Fair Value of £1.85 and focused on different pressures. Rising regulatory scrutiny of packaging and heavier reliance on a small group of UK retailers were treated as key risks to earnings stability.

What The Results Changed For The Greencore Group Thesis

Greencore Group raised profit guidance as volumes ran ahead of the sector and highlighted progress integrating Bakkavor, which supported the optimistic efficiency story. The same period brought harder figures to weigh. Revenue moved from £922m in H1 2025 to £1,318m in H1 2026, while net income swung from a £19.8m profit to a £34.8m loss and net margin fell to 2.6% below zero. The evidence cut both ways.

The whole episode turned on one assumption. Cost and automation programs were expected to protect profitability. The simple check at any other business is whether higher sales are matched by a net margin that holds or improves in the reported numbers.

What You Would Be Paying For In Greencore Group Today

Greencore Group now trades at £3.01, after a 35.1% gain over the past year from £2.29. The bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St sees its Fair Value below that level, arguing the recent price already bakes in a lot of the improvement story.

The same Narrative leans on a simple question: Do you believe Greencore can turn Bakkavor synergies and its Making Business Easier and automation work into steady margins and free cash flow, despite cash exceptionals, working capital strain and ongoing inflation pressure?

"While management targets at least £80m of annual cost synergies from the Bakkavor combination with specific phasing through 2029, the recent negative £76m free cash flow on a continuing basis and sizeable working capital outflow of about £86m highlight that integration and alignment of terms may absorb more cash and time than expected, which could hold back free cash flow conversion and delay any improvement in net margins."

data.title: Solstad Maritime (OB:SOMA) Posted Healthy Earnings But There Are Some Other Factors To Be Aware Of
data.description:
Solstad Maritime ASA's (OB:SOMA) robust earnings report didn't manage to move the market for its stock. Our analysis suggests that this might be because shareholders have noticed some concerning underlying factors.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

An Unusual Tax Situation

Solstad Maritime reported a tax benefit of US$30m, which is well worth noting. This is of course a bit out of the ordinary, given it is more common for companies to be paying tax than receiving tax benefits! Of course, prima facie it's great to receive a tax benefit. However, the devil in the detail is that these kind of benefits only impact in the year they are booked, and are often one-off in nature. In the likely event the tax benefit is not repeated, we'd expect to see its statutory profit levels drop, at least in the absence of strong growth. While we think it's good that the company has booked a tax benefit, it does mean that there's every chance the statutory profit will come in a lot higher than it would be if the income was adjusted for one-off factors.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On Solstad Maritime's Profit Performance

Solstad Maritime reported that it received a tax benefit, rather than paid tax, in its last report. As a result we don't think its profit result, which includes that tax-boost, is a good guide to its sustainable profit levels. Because of this, we think that it may be that Solstad Maritime's statutory profits are better than its underlying earnings power. The good news is that its earnings per share increased slightly in the last year. At the end of the day, it's essential to consider more than just the factors above, if you want to understand the company properly. If you'd like to know more about Solstad Maritime as a business, it's important to be aware of any risks it's facing. Case in point: We've spotted 2 warning signs for Solstad Maritime you should be mindful of and 1 of them shouldn't be ignored.

This note has only looked at a single factor that sheds light on the nature of Solstad Maritime's profit. But there is always more to discover if you are capable of focussing your mind on minutiae. data.title: Analysts Are Updating Their New Wave Group AB (publ) (STO:NEWA B) Estimates After Its Third-Quarter Results
data.description:
It's been a good week for New Wave Group AB (publ) (STO:NEWA B) shareholders, because the company has just released its latest third-quarter results, and the shares gained 2.9% to kr104. The result was positive overall - although revenues of kr2.7b were in line with what the analysts predicted, New Wave Group surprised by delivering a statutory profit of kr1.77 per share, modestly greater than expected. Earnings are an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance, look at what the analysts are forecasting for next year, and see if there's been a change in sentiment towards the company. So we collected the latest post-earnings statutory consensus estimates to see what could be in store for next year.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Taking into account the latest results, the most recent consensus for New Wave Group from four analysts is for revenues of kr12.6b in 2027. If met, it would imply a meaningful 17% increase on its revenue over the past 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to surge 28% to kr8.41. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of kr12.8b and earnings per share (EPS) of kr8.72 in 2027. The analysts seem to have become a little more negative on the business after the latest results, given the small dip in their earnings per share numbers for next year.

See our latest analysis for New Wave Group

The consensus price target held steady at kr114, with the analysts seemingly voting that their lower forecast earnings are not expected to lead to a lower stock price in the foreseeable future. Fixating on a single price target can be unwise though, since the consensus target is effectively the average of analyst price targets. As a result, some investors like to look at the range of estimates to see if there are any diverging opinions on the company's valuation. There are some variant perceptions on New Wave Group, with the most bullish analyst valuing it at kr130 and the most bearish at kr105 per share. Still, with such a tight range of estimates, it suggeststhe analysts have a pretty good idea of what they think the company is worth.

Of course, another way to look at these forecasts is to place them into context against the industry itself. It's clear from the latest estimates that New Wave Group's rate of growth is expected to accelerate meaningfully, with the forecast 13% annualised revenue growth to the end of 2027 noticeably faster than its historical growth of 7.5% p.a. over the past five years. Compare this with other companies in the same industry, which are forecast to grow their revenue 6.1% annually. Factoring in the forecast acceleration in revenue, it's pretty clear that New Wave Group is expected to grow much faster than its industry.

The Bottom Line

The biggest concern is that the analysts reduced their earnings per share estimates, suggesting business headwinds could lay ahead for New Wave Group. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. The consensus price target held steady at kr114, with the latest estimates not enough to have an impact on their price targets.

Following on from that line of thought, we think that the long-term prospects of the business are much more relevant than next year's earnings. We have forecasts for New Wave Group going out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here.

data.title: Earnings Miss: InfraCom Group AB (publ) Missed EPS By 23% And Analysts Are Revising Their Forecasts
data.description:
It's been a mediocre week for InfraCom Group AB (publ) (NGM:INFRA) shareholders, with the stock dropping 16% to kr9.50 in the week since its latest second-quarter results. Statutory earnings per share fell badly short of expectations, coming in at kr0.31, some 23% below analyst forecasts, although revenues were okay, approximately in line with analyst estimates at kr198m. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. We've gathered the most recent statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their earnings models, following these results.

Taking into account the latest results, InfraCom Group's two analysts currently expect revenues in 2026 to be kr816.9m, approximately in line with the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are expected to plunge 36% to kr1.21 in the same period. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of kr813.6m and earnings per share (EPS) of kr1.37 in 2026. So there's definitely been a decline in sentiment after the latest results, noting the real cut to new EPS forecasts.

Check out our latest analysis for InfraCom Group

The average price target fell 22% to kr19.80, with reduced earnings forecasts clearly tied to a lower valuation estimate.

Taking a look at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can understand these forecasts is to see how they compare to both past performance and industry growth estimates. These estimates imply that revenue is expected to slow, with a forecast annualised decline of 2.7% by the end of 2026. This indicates a significant reduction from annual growth of 23% over the last five years. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in the same industry are forecast to see their revenue grow 4.5% annually for the foreseeable future. It's pretty clear that InfraCom Group's revenues are expected to perform substantially worse than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing to take away is that the analysts downgraded their earnings per share estimates, showing that there has been a clear decline in sentiment following these results. On the plus side, there were no major changes to revenue estimates; although forecasts imply they will perform worse than the wider industry. The consensus price target fell measurably, with the analysts seemingly not reassured by the latest results, leading to a lower estimate of InfraCom Group's future valuation.

Keeping that in mind, we still think that the longer term trajectory of the business is much more important for investors to consider. At least one analyst has provided forecasts out to 2028, which can be seen for free on our platform here.
